messages:
maya: FYI, after promoting v4-tokenizer to prod we started seeing a P99 latency jump (~3x) on short-seq requests around 10:20 UTC. KV cache miss rate also spiked.
runtime-bot: ALERT: high-latency-detection triggered on cluster-gpu-3 — link: https://perf.redwood/incident/8432 :rotating_light:
kevin: can you paste a short trace or hotspot? is this only on a single model? @maya
maya: only on the transformer-small model variant that we rolled with tokenizer v4. Quick paste of profiler output from the period:

```
[10:21:12] trace_id=abc123 kernel_select: chosen=matmul_dense reason=seq_len_bucket=8 pad_ratio=0.05
[10:21:12] trace_id=abc123 kv_cache: miss_rate=0.72 hits=28 misses=72
[10:21:12] batcher: avg_batch_size=1.6 frequent_singletons=0.64
[10:21:12] hw_metrics: gpu_util=52% steam_warps=some
```

maya: kernel_select logs look wrong — we expected fused_attention for these short-seq requests but it's picking the dense matmul path.
oscar: noticed a big rise in tiny requests after the tokenizer change — tokenization now emits many 3-8 token payloads instead of 15-30. Batcher saw singletons up from 22%->64% which kills batching efficiency.
kevin: that could also change seq-len distribution used by the kernel selection heuristic. maybe the heuristic uses median seq_len and mis-buckets.
anika: checking the kernel selection rule set now. config snippet:

```
kernel_selector:
  pad_threshold: 0.8 # intent was 0.08 during canary
  seqlen_buckets: [0-16,17-64,65-256]
```

anika: uh that pad_threshold was a typo in the rollout config (decimal vs percent). it's basically forcing selection for dense matmul when pad_ratio < 0.8 which matches these short requests.
sam: also saw KV cache churn — tokenizer change changed input prefixing so cache keys are less shared, hits drop. combined with tiny batches, we hit more kernel warmups and less reuse.
kevin: can we reproduce on staging by hitting the new tokenizer and measuring pad_ratio->kernel mapping? if it's config we can revert fast.
maya: repro on staging is fast. running a short sweep now with synthetic 3-8 token feeds.
oscar: staging shows the same kernel_select path and batcher avg_batch_size=1.7. Perf regression local estimate ~2.8x P99.
kevin: rollback v4-tokenizer for the small model in prod? or hotfix to kernel selector to ignore pad_threshold if seq_len < 16? which is safer?
anika: safer to patch kernel selector (hotfix) because other models benefit from the tokenizer change. patch: change pad_threshold from 0.8 -> 0.08 and add special-case: if median_seq_len < 12 then prefer fused_attention.
maya: agree, hotfix and a canary roll for 30m. I'll open rollout.
deploy-bot: START_ROLLOUT: kernel-selector-hotfix -> prod (id=rz-129) by maya. Canary targets: 5% conv gpupool.
sam: note: we should also add a KV cache key normalization follow-up. the tokenizer introduces a prefix token that changes cache keys; that reduces hit rate. filing issue after hotfix.
kevin: good. assignables: maya (rollout), anika (kernel-selector hotfix PR + test), oscar (batcher metric dashboard update), sam (KV cache follow-up). i'll own postmortem.
maya: canary results after 10m: P99 back to baseline ~1.05x, avg_batch_size up to 4.2 in canary pool, kv_cache miss_rate down from 0.72 -> 0.28.
anika: hotfix PR merged and rolled to 100% after successful canary. PR: https://git.redwood/pr/2248
deploy-bot: ROLLOUT_COMPLETE: kernel-selector-hotfix -> prod (id=rz-129)
maya: issuing rollback of tokenizer v4 for the small model as a precaution for next few hours while we monitor the cache hit shape.
deploy-bot: ROLLBACK: tokenizer-v4 -> previous (id=tz-78) initiated by maya.
oscar: creating dashboard panel to show "short-seq rate" and kernel_choice distribution by seq_len bucket.
kevin: good, also add alert if avg_batch_size drops below 2 for >5m.
sam: filing KV normalization ticket: https://tickets.redwood/INF-918 — includes proposed key canonicalization and eval harness.
maya: postmortem notes: immediate cause = bad pad_threshold in rollout config + tokenizer shift to shorter outputs causing batching+kv churn. Secondary = lack of guardrail alerting on avg_batch_size drop.
kevin: action items: 1) add config lint to catch decimal/percent mismatches (anika) 2) add avg_batch_size alert (oscar) 3) KV key normalization work (sam) 4) add canary synthetic seqlen sweep to rollout checklist (maya)
maya: thanks all. I'll compile a short incident summary for oncall and stakeholders.
runtime-bot: INCIDENT: 8432 status=resolved severity=moderate lead=kevin summary="Kernel selection + KV churn after tokenizer rollout" tags=[kernel,kvcache,tokenizer]
maya: closing thread, will paste the postmortem link when ready.
